candidates.label: MusicRecording
candidates.comment: A MusicRecording, as a CreativeWork, is a recorded performance of a musical composition, usually a single song. Also called music track, song recording, audio track. Examples: 'Yesterday' by The Beatles (the recorded version), a single from an album, a demo track. Distinct from MusicComposition, which is the abstract musical work.

candidates.label: InstantaneousEvent
candidates.comment: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.

candidates.label: BroadcastEvent
candidates.comment: A BroadcastEvent is a PublicationEvent representing an event that is transmitted over the air or online. Also called live broadcast, streamed event, televised event, radio broadcast. Examples: a live news report, a sports game broadcast, a concert livestream.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

types.embedding_query_text: Rate: A measure, quantity, or frequency, typically one measured against another quantity or measure. Also called Ratio, Proportion, Speed. Examples: twice as fast as the global average.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: A rate is a measurable amount, making schema.org/Quantity the best fit.

mentions: twice as fast as the global average

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

types.embedding_query_text: WeatherPhenomenon: A specific atmospheric event or process that occurs in the weather. Also called Atmospheric event, Meteorological phenomenon. Examples: increased summer heatwaves.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.justification: A weather phenomenon is a happening, making schema.org/Event a suitable general type.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: SpecialAnnouncement
candidates.comment: A date-stamped textual information update from a locally-oriented organization, often related to urgent crisis situations, including contextual web links and structured data. Also called public notice, crisis update, community alert, emergency announcement. Examples: a school closure announcement due to weather, a pharmacy's updated operating hours during a pandemic, a local government's public health advisory.

candidates.label: OnDemandEvent
candidates.comment: An OnDemandEvent, as a PublicationEvent, is a publication event where a program is available on-demand. Also called catch-up TV, podcast release, streaming event. Examples: a TV show episode available for streaming after broadcast, a podcast episode release, a movie available for rent online. Distinct from BroadcastEvent, which is a live or scheduled transmission.

candidates.label: EventStatusType
candidates.comment: An EventStatusType is a StatusEnumeration whose instances represent various states an Event may be in. Also called event state, status of event. Examples: EventScheduled, EventCancelled, EventPostponed, EventRescheduled.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

types.embedding_query_text: Impact: The effect or influence of one thing on another. Also called Effect, Consequence, Result. Examples: greater pressure on Europe's water supply.

chosen_type.label: Impact
chosen_type.definition: The effect or influence of one thing on another.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type represents a general impact or effect; Thing is the most general parent.

mentions: greater pressure on Europe's water supply

candidates.label: ConsumeAction
candidates.comment: The act of ingesting or utilizing information, resources, or food. Also called consumption, utilizing, ingesting, using. Examples: Reading a book, eating a meal, watching a movie, using electricity. Distinct from Action, which is a general activity.

candidates.label: TradeAction
candidates.comment: The act of exchanging goods or services for monetary compensation. Also called commerce, transaction, selling. Examples: a business selling products to customers, a consultant providing services for a fee, an artist selling their artwork.

candidates.label: UseAction
candidates.comment: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose or function. Also called utilize, employ, operate. Examples: using a tool to fix something, consuming food, wearing clothes.

candidates.label: AssessAction
candidates.comment: An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate. Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.embedding_query_text: WeatherEvent: A specific occurrence or incident related to weather. Also called Meteorological event, Climate event. Examples: This summer's record-breaking temperatures.

chosen_type.label: WeatherEvent
chosen_type.definition: A specific occurrence or incident related to weather.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type specifically represents a general weather-related incident; Event is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: BroadcastEvent
candidates.comment: A BroadcastEvent is a PublicationEvent representing an event that is transmitted over the air or online. Also called live broadcast, streamed event, televised event, radio broadcast. Examples: a live news report, a sports game broadcast, a concert livestream.

candidates.label: FoodEvent
candidates.comment: A FoodEvent is an Event centered around food and drink. Also called culinary event, gastronomic event, food festival. Examples: A wine tasting, a cooking class, a food fair, a restaurant week promotion.

types.embedding_query_text: Descriptor: A word or phrase used to describe something. Also called Attribute, Characteristic, Qualifier. Examples: unprecedented, underestimate, very high.

chosen_type.label: DefinedTerm
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/DefinedTerm best fits the OIE_TYPE definition for a word or phrase used to describe something.

candidates.label: DefinedTerm
candidates.comment: An intangible entity representing a word, phrase, or acronym with a formal definition, often used in glossaries or classification schemes. Also called Glossary entry, vocabulary term, classification code, concept. Examples: "ISBN" (International Standard Book Number), "HTTP" (Hypertext Transfer Protocol), "Organic" (as a food label). Distinct from DefinedTermSet, which is a collection of such terms.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

types.embedding_query_text: CauseOfDeath: The specific injury or disease that leads to death. Also called Manner of death, Fatal cause. Examples: Drowning deaths.

chosen_type.label: MedicalCondition
chosen_type.justification: Causes of death are often medical conditions or injuries, making schema.org/MedicalCondition the best general fit.

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: DDxElement
candidates.comment: A DDxElement is an alternative, closely-related medical condition considered during differential diagnosis, along with the distinguishing signs. Also called differential diagnosis item, alternative diagnosis, rule-out condition. Examples: Considering "strep throat" as a DDxElement for a patient presenting with a sore throat and fever, alongside "common cold."

candidates.label: LoseAction
candidates.comment: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity or contest. Also called suffer defeat, be beaten, fail to win. Examples: losing a game, being defeated in an election, failing a competition. Distinct from AchieveAction, which is a broader category for actions that result in an outcome.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

types.embedding_query_text: Risk: A situation involving exposure to danger. Also called Hazard, Peril, Vulnerability. Examples: risk of an outbreak.

chosen_type.label: MedicalRiskFactor
chosen_type.justification: schema.org/MedicalRiskFactor is the best fit for the concept of a situation involving exposure to danger, even if not strictly medical.

Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: PreventionIndication
candidates.comment: A PreventionIndication is a MedicalIndication for preventing an underlying medical condition, symptom, or disease. Also called prophylactic indication, preventative use. Examples: a vaccine for measles prevention, a medication to prevent migraines, dietary changes to prevent heart disease, exercise to prevent diabetes.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskEstimator
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any rule set or interactive tool used to estimate the risk of developing a complication or condition. Also called risk assessment tool, prognosis predictor, clinical risk model. Examples: a calculator for stroke risk, a scoring system for surgical complications. Distinct from MedicalRiskFactor, which is a single factor increasing risk.

types.embedding_query_text: Forecast: A prediction or estimate of future events, especially weather. Also called Prediction, Projection, Outlook. Examples: possibility of another heatwave.

chosen_type.label: Forecast
chosen_type.definition: A prediction or estimate of future events or conditions.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type specifically represents a general forecast; Intangible is a suitable parent for a prediction.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

types.embedding_query_text: Observation: The action or process of observing something or someone carefully or in order to gain information. Also called Finding, Discovery, Note. Examples: clear increase.

chosen_type.label: Observation
chosen_type.justification: The schema.org/Observation type perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE definition and mention.

candidates.label: Observation
candidates.comment: An Observation is an intangible entity used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time, often quantitative. Also called measurement, data point, recorded value. Examples: a temperature reading, a stock price at a specific time, a survey response. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which is a specific type of observation with a numerical value and unit.

candidates.label: DiscoverAction
candidates.comment: A find action representing the act of finding or uncovering an object or information. Also called Find, uncover, locate, detect, unearth. Examples: Discovering a new species, finding a lost item, uncovering a historical artifact, detecting a bug in software. Distinct from FindAction, which is a broader category for seeking something.

candidates.label: TrackAction
candidates.comment: The act of monitoring an inanimate object for updates or changes in its location or status. Also called monitoring, tracking, observing. Examples: tracking a package delivery, monitoring a flight's progress, tracking a lost phone.

candidates.label: WatchAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming dynamic or moving visual content. Also called view, observe, see. Examples: watching a movie, watching a live sports broadcast, watching a video tutorial.

candidates.label: FindAction
candidates.comment: FindAction is an Action representing the act of locating an object. Also called discover, locate, unearth. Examples: Finding a lost key, discovering a new species, locating a specific document, unearthing an artifact. Distinct from SearchAction, which is generally a precursor to FindAction.

types.embedding_query_text: Heatwave: A prolonged period of abnormally hot weather. Also called Hot spell, Heat wave, Scorcher. Examples: heatwave, record-breaking European heatwave.

chosen_type.label: Heatwave
chosen_type.definition: A prolonged period of abnormally hot weather.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type specifically represents a heatwave; WeatherEvent is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle that provides historical context, definitions, or detailed explanations on a specific topic. Also called explainer article, backgrounder, FAQ document. Examples: "An explainer on climate change", "A detailed history of the European Union", "FAQ about blockchain technology". Distinct from NewsArticle, which reports on current events.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

types.embedding_query_text: Characteristic Examples: fastest warming continent.

chosen_type.label: Characteristic
chosen_type.definition: A distinguishing quality or feature of something.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type is general enough for 'Characteristic'; Property is a suitable parent for an attribute.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: GeoCoordinates
candidates.comment: GeoCoordinates is a StructuredValue representing the geographic coordinates of a place or event, typically latitude and longitude. Also called geographic location, GPS coordinates, spatial coordinates. Examples: Latitude 34.0522, Longitude -118.2437 (for Los Angeles), a specific point on a map, the coordinates of an event venue.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
candidates.comment: An EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration is an EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration listing the EU energy efficiency classes A-G, A+, A++, and A+++ as defined in EU directive 2017/1369. Also called EU energy rating, European energy class. Examples: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA+++, EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryG.
